text: Formed in the late 1980s, the Kaska Dena Drummers are a locally well-known musical group that perform traditional songs. Historically, the Kaska also participated in the Potlatch — a cultural gift-giving ceremony. Potlatch was banned by the Indian Act until 1951. Many Indigenous communities have since resumed the practice. Kaska is a Dene (Athabaskan) language spoken primarily in the communities of Ross River, Watson Lake, Upper Liard, Lower Post, Fireside, Good Hope Lake (see also Fort Good Hope), Dease Lake and Muncho Lake.
